SMTO-RST-0003 — SMTO couldn't tell which saved history this task belongs to

GUID: 57893255-9bc8-443f-b401-bf2f063acc97
Slug: run-journal-identity-invalid
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't match this task to one trustworthy saved history, so it stopped instead of guessing. Some of the task's work may already have happened before it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task's conversation and read its last results to see which steps finished. SMTO stopped without knowing for sure where the task got to, so some changes may already be done.
  2. If the task could have changed things outside SMTO, such as files or messages, check those directly. Check whether your action already happened, so asking again doesn't repeat a change.
  3. Then send a new message describing only what's still left to do. A new message starts a fresh history, so it doesn't depend on the one SMTO couldn't identify.

What success looks like

  • The new message runs without this error and nothing is done twice.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before you try anything again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; this is a problem inside SMTO. Don't delete the conversation or the task meanwhile, because its saved records are needed to investigate.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Journal resolution found an explicit journal ID that contradicts its durable binding, an existing or resumed run with no binding, or saved run state missing its journal metadata.

What this means

  • Journal resolution finds contradictory explicit/durable IDs, an unbound existing/resumed run, or a saved state missing required journal metadata. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Journal resolution finds contradictory explicit/durable IDs, an unbound existing/resumed run, or a saved state missing required journal metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect durable binding and saved journal metadata without synthesizing an ID to satisfy validation.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Investigate resolve_native_journal_id, MemoryRunStore._bind/decode and RunStore.decode for the run: compare the state's journal_id with its native_run_journals row. Preserve the saved run, journal and error details for investigation; reconcile external state through a new inspection before further mutations, and do not synthesize journal identities or replay saved work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original binding is restored through supported recovery or external state is inspected before new work.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
